title: Ua ʻŌhiʻa Lani: An Image to Celebrate Gemini North’s 25th Anniversary
caption: The nebula and star cluster NGC 6820, imaged by the Gemini North telescope
credit: International Gemini Observatory/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA. Image Processing: J. Miller & M. Rodriguez (International Gemini Observatory/NSF NOIRLab), T.A. Rector (University of Alaska Anchorage/NSF NOIRLab), M. Zamani (NSF NOIRLab)

recognition.text: Official NSF NOIRLab / Gemini press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: This Gemini North image shows NGC 6820, an emission nebula paired with an open star cluster, in the direction of Vulpecula. Students in Hawai‘i voted to choose it as the subject of an image celebrating 25 years since the International Gemini Observatory was completed.

The picture's name, Ua ʻŌhiʻa Lani, means the Heavenly ʻŌhiʻa Rains and comes from a traditional Hawaiian story about the ʻŌhiʻa forests. An emission nebula is a cloud of gas that glows because energetic light from hot young stars excites it, while an open cluster is a loose group of stars born together from the same cloud. When the two appear together, the young cluster is often the source of the light that makes the nebula shine.

NSF NOIRLab operates the International Gemini Observatory, which receives part of its funding from the U.S. National Science Foundation. Its Gemini North telescope recorded NGC 6820 with the Gemini Multi-Object Spectrograph through g, r, i and hydrogen-alpha filters.

understand.summary: Taken in visible light with the Gemini Multi-Object Spectrograph on Gemini North through g, r, i and hydrogen-alpha filters. The colour mapping isn't published.
understand.eye: The hydrogen-alpha filter isolates the red glow of hydrogen, and the long exposure gathers far more light than the eye could.
